title: A 4-week study plan
lines: Four weeks is a short runway. It works best if you already have a fair base in English and high-school math and need to sharpen skills, learn the format and build pacing. Plan on about 2 hours a day on weekdays and 3-4 hours on one weekend day, which adds up to roughly 55 hours.
## Principles for a short plan
- Find your weak topics fast, then spend most of your time on them.
- Learn the format and pacing early; they are quick wins.
- Do vocabulary every day in short sessions, not in big blocks.
- Take a full mock test every weekend.
! With only four weeks, do not try to cover every topic equally. Points come fastest from weak topics that appear often, such as Text Completion, reading and core algebra.
## Before you start (day 1)
- Read the guide articles in "The exam" group: format, question types and scoring.
- Take Mock Test 1 under real conditions, essay included. This is your baseline.
- Open the Progress tab and write down your five weakest topics, plus your estimated Verbal and Quant scores.
## Week 1: foundations and diagnosis
- Daily: 15 minutes of vocabulary flashcards (about 20 new words, plus review).
- Verbal: lessons and practice sets for Text Completion and Sentence Equivalence.
- Quant: lessons and practice sets for number properties, arithmetic and percents, and the two weakest Quant topics from your mock.
- Read the strategy articles on time management and on guessing and marking.
- Write one practice essay under the 30-minute timer and rate it against the model essay.
- Weekend: take Mock Test 2. Compare section 1 accuracy with Mock Test 1.
## Week 2: weak topics
- Daily: vocabulary flashcards, now reviewing missed words first.
- Verbal: reading comprehension lessons and practice sets (short passages, long passages, arguments).
- Quant: algebra and word problems, then your next weakest Quant topic from the Progress tab.
- Redo any practice set where you scored below 70%, after rereading its lesson.
- Read the Verbal tips and Quant tips articles and try one technique on each set (prediction in Verbal, plugging in or back-solving in Quant).
- Write one practice essay and use the template from the essay article.
- Weekend: take Mock Test 3. Review every wrong answer and every guessed answer.
## Week 3: pressure and mixed practice
- Daily: vocabulary flashcards.
- Practice sets with the timer for every topic still marked weak.
- Quant: geometry and data interpretation lessons and practice sets, if not already done.
- Mixed review: one Verbal and one Quant practice set from different topics every day, to practice switching.
- Write one practice essay.
- Midweek: take Mock Test 4 under real conditions.
- Weekend: take Mock Test 5. Use the checkpoints from the time management article.
## Week 4: polish and rest
- Days 1-3: return to the two topics where your accuracy is still lowest. Redo their practice sets and reread their lessons.
- Day 3 or 4: take Mock Test 6 at the same time of day as your real test. This is your last full mock.
- Days 5-6: light review only: flashcards, a few explanations from earlier mocks, the essay template.
- Read the test day and test anxiety articles. Prepare your ID, route or room.
- Day before the test: no new material. A short walk, an early night.
## How to know you are on track
- Your section 1 accuracy rises from mock to mock.
- You finish every section with every question answered.
- The weak-topic list in the Progress tab gets shorter or changes.

If after Mock Test 4 your estimates are still far below your goal, consider whether a longer plan and a later test date would serve you better. The 8-week plan builds the same skills with more time for practice.
